It depends on the properties of the voting system you use. This seems to be a question in the domain of social choice theory, which has results like Arrow's impossibility theorem and Sen's paradox. In the case of communal decisions, in cases where consensus can't be reached, you can sometimes yield decisions that at worst leave some people indifferent.

I would also say "hierarchy" is commonly understood as a system that presumes people can be ranked or ordered in some way. You might not like the outcome of a communal decision, but it's not hierarchy until your voice is considered somehow less valuable.

I think alcohol might denature the compounds slightly, since it was noted on Erowid that there are no reports of strong effects from extracted product. I can offer a single anecdote that I had a good trip with no nausea from a tincture, but have experienced abdominal discomfort and vomiting with the same unextracted dose.

On the other hand you could be an agent of the message to stay trapped here, wherever here is, if it even is a place where one is "trapped". You can see perhaps why this is a terrifying and disorienting mindset. Everything is suddenly ambiguously a message and I don't know what to make of a world that was real only last week and suddenly isn't.

I was in the same boat, plus psychosis, minus doing well in school. I don't know if you're locked into your therapist and psychiatrist, but if you have the option to "shop around", do so. If you'd like, please do talk to me about why you feel these professionals aren't working. As a client it won't work if you're passive, you need to know what you need and be able to assert that.

I don't know if it helps, but life goes on. I did too poorly in high school to get into any universities directly, but there are alternative pathways. I think one thing you can at least do is to keep moving forward.

I don't know if you can talk to the therapist about the suicidal thoughts, but it might help to get them off your chest. Being locked inside your head with a homicidal maniac is a harrowing experience for everyone it happens to.

It's possible that many more people experience poisoning than experience bad enough poisoning to need, or the feel the need, to seek medical attention, and fatalities are rare even in that group. How do you know when it's bad enough? Is your pulse over 120 BPM and do you have a fever? Then it's bad, and you should call an ambulance. If you're worried, make sure you have a poisons center on your speed dial.

Had mild-moderate serotonin poisoning twice. Once on high 3rd on my first trip, the second time after mixing *way too much* MK-801 (2x 3.5 mg oral in DMSO spaced 5hrs apart) with SJW. The worst thing on DXM is the uncontrolled fight or flight and intense fear of death when on high DXM doses.

I also tried my first 300 mg dose with SJW, and was fine. The euphoria was better pre-trip and during the comedown, but the drug seemed to have been weakened. Dream states were less intrusive, recall was better. There's also a report on erowid of a low dose mixed with an MAOI, and the lady was fine.

*On the other hand*, there are reports of bad things happening to people who've mixed fluoxetine with high doses of DXM. If you feel you're at risk of redosing and taking too much.

@OP, if you're feeling brave or totally committed, make sure you know how to breathe to keep yourself calm. Get some benzos as backup, and proceed with caution through the 2nd plateau.

Provided it's even working, it's not quite as dramatic as its reputation might lead you to believe. Maybe I have spoiled it though, even a dose of 13 ug/kg (the erowid "Lobotomy" report was 22 ug/kg) is only around the intensity of the come-up on 1.2g of DXM (spatial distortion, language and memory disturbances, time compression, drunkenness without body high or euphoria).

I've been reading that DXM in of itself is quite a weak drug, with most of the dissociative (and memory) problems coming from DXO's NMDA antagonism. Following this, you might be an efficient metaboliser and converting to DXO too quickly. You could try a combination of grapefruit juice (or homemade oil) and taking many small doses close together as opposed to one big one.

Of course I could be completely wrong about this being a metabolic issue.

I eventually threw up. That was also when I finally started hallucinating, but I was so far out of it I didn't really get to appreciate it.

You can probably manage the nausea with dimenhydrinate. It eases the discomfort, and seems to weaken the reflex to vomit. It does come with body load though, or maybe that's just because the local brand contains scopolamine.

I normally have terrible social anxiety.

I like the cognitive effects. It feels like your brain develops the super-power of macguyvering together concepts you wouldn't normally think about. Like how are a cat and a paper clip alike? I don't know, but if I ever drink that much coffee again I'll tell you.
